chapter: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
title: Why Cab Calloway's band was the height of the band business
summary: Danny says Cab paid better, bought uniforms, traveled first class, and Mr. Wright was like a daddy to the band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well, what are you all doing down here now? You came back to... We never did get into Cab Calloway's days, did we, Danny.

Well, ...(?)... decided to come back to New Orleans. But like, I'd been with Cab Calloway, and this was the height you could go in the band business, with the big Swing bands... It was the height, the most highly respected
and there was. And in comparison, when I'd hear other guys talk about other bands, Cab was more liberal and more free with his money and paid you better...
You traveled first-class. You never had the idea of paying for your own uniform.
He bought the uniforms. And he traveled first-class at all times.
If you got pushed for some money on the road, you could always go to Mister Wright, who we called our Daddy.
That's right. He's still living, you know.
We hear from him periodically. Fine man.
And we traveled first-class. You reached the height of music when you joined Cab at that time.
